A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MEBench and provide readable methods, results, figures, tables and appendices. Their corresponding scientific content can be matched despite formatting and organizational changes.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original MEBench experiments, including accuracy, entity-attribution scores, subtask performance and entity-density analyses.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original empirical results in Tables 3-4 and Figure 3, including comparisons across models and entity-density groups.

M1.justification: The Wikipedia/SPARQL collection, information extraction, template-based question generation and SQL-derived answering pipeline remains intact. The hierarchical RAG wording elaborates the earlier structured RAG description without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 4,780-question benchmark covering 241 topics, three reasoning categories, eight task types and three entity-density groups. No additional dataset or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 3-4 retain the same eight configurations: GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, Llama-3-Instruct and fine-tuned Llama-3-Instruct, each with and without RAG. Newly cited systems are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The 3,406/1,374 training/test split, QLoRA setup, chunk size of 1,024, top-five retrieval and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Both assess statistical-task column/method selection rather than numerical computation and require exact tuple matching for EA-F1.

E4.justification: The RAG and fine-tuning comparisons, eight-subtask analysis and entity-density breakdowns are retained. The new limitations discussion introduces no additional ablation, robustness experiment or case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or a significance-test procedure. Both retain the same assertion of a statistically significant performance margin in Section 4.2.

E6.justification: Section 4.2 corrects the prose accuracy for Llama-3-Instruct with RAG from 31.6% to 32.5%, matching Table 3 in both versions. All 32 accuracy rows, eight EA-F1 scores and the Figure 3 subtask plot remain unchanged; this is a reporting correction.

T1.justification: The exact-tuple EA-F1 definition and Appendix A.1's SPARQL refinement stopping condition, including the 0.98 threshold, are retained. Neither version supplies additional theorems, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the multi-entity benchmark, task taxonomy, entity-level evaluation and scalable construction pipeline. The headline finding that leading models achieve approximately 59% accuracy is unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 5 substantially expands qualifications of the benchmark: limited dynamic or temporal interactions, curated documents that underrepresent real-world noise, and EA-F1 potentially undervaluing partially correct reasoning. These add applicability and score-interpretation boundaries absent from v1's discussion of model shortcomings.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data repository footnote and a more explicit RAG description. It removes the API code example, the GPT-4 fine-tuning qualifier in Appendix A.1.2, and v1 Appendix A.4's two-reviewer, consensus and calibration details. These change documentation without establishing altered implementation or review procedures.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work substantially expand cited literature, including SRAG, CRAG, Symphony, text-to-SQL, visualization and agent systems. This broadens the research context toward data science and databases while retaining the central cross-document, entity-dense benchmark-gap argument.

P1.justification: v2 edits the introduction and conclusion, condenses the individual task explanations, and moves quality control from Section 3.2.3 to Appendix A.2.2. It also reorganizes appendix headings and updates authorship, while retaining most of the narrative structure and prose.

P2.justification: All six tables and three figures are retained. v2 changes typography, publication formatting and display placement, rearranges Figure 1's labels, and lightly redraws Figure 2. Figure 3 contains the identical plot, displayed at a different size and position.

improvement.justification: The new limitations section improves interpretation of benchmark scope and EA-F1 scores, and the corrected 32.5% result resolves a prose/table inconsistency. The code/data-access statement is also useful. These gains are limited by unchanged empirical and statistical support, removal of some reproducibility details, and an unresolved citation in Section 2.2.
